themes_detail.label: Tree Die-Off Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying trees complaints spiked to 5 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% spike (z-score: 6.29)—suggesting a rapid environmental or pest event affecting Upper West Side street canopy.
evidence: 5 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score 6.29)
Spike is statistically severe and emerged only this week, suggesting acute trigger rather than seasonal trend
Aligns with community board priority: repeated budget requests for park reconstruction and tree maintenance
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept on root cause: disease outbreak, pest infestation, infrastructure conflict, or weather event?
Map complaint locations to identify if die-off is concentrated in specific neighborhood blocks or park areas
Investigate if this is part of citywide tree health crisis or isolated to Upper West Side

themes_detail.label: Curb Degradation Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped to 17 exactly 2 weeks ago versus 2.9 per week baseline—a 491% spike (z-score: 13.41)—indicating possible widespread street infrastructure failure tied to construction activity or freeze-thaw cycle.
evidence: 17 curb condition complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.9 weekly baseline (491% spike, z-score 13.41—highest on severity scale)
1,185 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (1,089 alterations) suggest heavy construction activity that may be damaging street infrastructure
Curb failure compounds with illegal parking (1,498 complaints in 90 days) as vehicles damage weakened curbs further
reporting_angles: Cross-reference spike locations with active DOB permits to determine if construction dust/vibration is damaging curbs
Query DOB on whether they track construction-related curb damage claims or enforcement
Photograph affected blocks to document scope and severity for visual story component

themes_detail.label: Industrial Waste Dumping Spike
themes_detail.summary: Industrial waste complaints surged to 3 exactly 2 weeks ago versus 0.1 per week baseline—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting either illegal dumping operation, contractor non-compliance, or environmental enforcement gap.
evidence: 3 industrial waste complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score 8.69—most extreme proportional increase)
Spike is concentrated in single time period, suggesting discrete event rather than chronic problem
Community board has standing request for expanded code enforcement (DOHMH/DOB), indicating chronic enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: Identify the 3 complaint locations and investigate: Are they near active construction sites, waste transfer facilities, or food service operations?
Interview DSNY and DOE on whether they've issued violations or traced dumping to specific operators
Determine if complaints are from residents or businesses, and whether any health risks are documented

themes_detail.label: Street Vending Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 12 last week versus 3.6 per week baseline—a 231% spike (z-score: 6.36)—indicating either a new enforcement campaign, illegal vendor proliferation, or complaint saturation around specific locations.
evidence: 12 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 3.6 weekly baseline (231% spike, z-score 6.36)
Complements 1,498 illegal parking complaints over 90 days, suggesting broader street use conflict
Upper West Side has dense food service and retail, making vending density and enforcement activity visible
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD and DOC on whether a targeted enforcement operation was launched last week
Identify whether complaints are from residents objecting to vendors or from vendors objecting to enforcement
Determine if spike reflects actual vendor increase or just heightened complaint awareness

themes_detail.label: Day Care Facility Issues Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Day care complaints spiked to 3 last week versus 0.5 per week baseline—a 500% spike (z-score: 5.0)—indicating possible capacity strain, health/safety violations, or staffing problems at child care centers.
evidence: 3 day care complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score 5.0)
Spike is recent but limited sample size (n=3); may not yet represent trend, but timing is critical given child safety stakes
Community board priorities include health services expansion, suggesting pre-existing capacity concerns
reporting_angles: Obtain DOE child care facility database and cross-reference complaint addresses to identify which centers triggered reports
Interview DOE on complaint nature: Are these licensing violations, health/safety, or capacity/waitlist issues?
Contact parent advocacy groups to determine if families are reporting unmet demand or quality problems
